title: September in Servo adds progress element and CSS enhancements
excerpt: Servo 0.7.0 ships the <progress> element, new CSS functions, and WebGL2 fixes among 527 commits.
body:
September 2026 saw Servo ship version 0.7.0, bundling 527 commits into a single update. The most visible changes are a native `<progress>` element, a one-call `roundRect()` method on the 2-D canvas, and a handful of accessibility, security, and WebAPI tweaks.

The release also upgrades the JavaScript engine to SpiderMonkey v153.3 and the graphics stack to mozangle v0.7, closing several upstream security bugs. By the end of this article you will know how to add a progress bar without a polyfill, draw rounded rectangles with a single call, enable precise accessibility geometry, and take advantage of new sanitization and database helpers.

## Native `<progress>` element, typed CSS arithmetic, and related UI tweaks  

Servo now implements the HTML 5 `<progress>` element. The tag accepts the standard `value` and `max` attributes, so a simple bar can be written as:

```html
<progress value="45" max="100"></progress>
```

No JavaScript shim is required, and the element participates in form submission and styling just like any other native control. Script can update the bar instantly:

```js
const bar = document.querySelector('progress')
bar.value = 73
```

The CSS engine gained typed arithmetic. The `calc()` function now works with typed values such as lengths, percentages, and angles, while the new `alpha()` function lets designers set opacity without wrapping a color in `rgba()`. Example:

```css
button {
  background-color: alpha(steelblue, 0.3);
  width: calc(50% - 2rem);
}
```

The release also adds the `:checked` pseudoclass and the `user-select` property, giving developers finer control over form state and text selection. For instance, `input:checked + label { font-weight: bold; }` now works out of the box. All of these changes are listed in the September Servo blog post [September in Servo: <progress>, rounded rectangles, and more](https://servo.org/blog/2026/11/05/september-in-servo/).

## Rounded rectangles on the 2-D canvas  

Before this release, drawing a rectangle with rounded corners required a manual path built from `arc()` and `lineTo()`. Servo 0.7.0 adds `CanvasRenderingContext2D.roundRect()`, which matches the signature of other drawing methods:

```js
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
ctx.fillStyle = '#4a90e2'
ctx.roundRect(20, 30, 200, 80, 10) // x, y, width, height, radius
ctx.fill()
```

The method accepts either a single radius or an array of four radii, mirroring the CSS `border-radius` syntax. This reduces boilerplate and eliminates subtle bugs around corner calculations. Existing code that already creates paths can switch to `roundRect()` with a single line change.

## WebGL2 conformance, graphics upgrades, and post-quantum crypto  

The WebGL2 implementation received a batch of conformance fixes behind the `--pref dom_webgl2_enabled` flag. The changes address edge-case rendering bugs such as incorrect texture filtering and missing framebuffer attachments. With SpiderMonkey v153.3 and mozangle v0.7 also upgraded, the graphics stack now benefits from upstream security patches and performance improvements.

Developers targeting high-performance visualizations can enable the flag and expect behavior that aligns more closely with the WebGL2 specification. The release notes list several pull requests (e.g., #48423, #48441) that fix specific shader compilation and draw-call ordering issues.

The WebCrypto module added support for the MLKEM768-X25519 algorithm, expanding the suite of post-quantum key-exchange primitives available to web applications. The implementation follows the standard API, so existing `subtle.encrypt` and `subtle.decrypt` calls can be switched to the new algorithm by changing the `name` parameter.

## Accessibility geometry, new accessibility events, and sanitization  

When the `--pref accessibility_enabled` preference is turned on, the accessibility tree now reports geometry bounds for inline elements. This means screen readers can obtain the exact on-screen rectangle of a text fragment, improving navigation and highlighting. Elements styled with `display: none` are explicitly marked as hidden, reducing noise for assistive tools.

Servo also introduced a new event API: `Servo::forward_accessibility_action`. Embedders can forward actions from external accessibility tools directly to the engine, enabling richer interaction models such as custom gestures or voice commands.

The Sanitizer API now accepts the `javascriptURLs` property, allowing developers to whitelist or strip `javascript:` URLs during sanitization. This gives finer-grained control over potentially unsafe content without discarding the entire element.

## IndexedDB improvements and media track handling  

IndexedDB received several usability upgrades:

* Duplicate index names in unrelated tables no longer cause errors.  
* `openCursor()` and `openKeyCursor()` are now available on `IDBIndex`.  
* Cursor methods `advance()`, `continue()`, and `continuePrimaryKey()` have been added to `IDBCursor`.

These changes simplify common database patterns such as paginated reads and key-only scans.

Closed-caption support for `<video>` elements has been tightened. Text tracks now fire `enter`, `exit`, and `cuechange` events, and the `textTracks` list returns a fully sorted collection. Adding cues to a track correctly updates the track’s state, and `VTTCue.getCueAsHTML()` is now functional. WebVTT parsing can recover from malformed cues, reducing playback failures on imperfect subtitle files.

## The takeaway  

Servo 0.7.0 delivers a native `<progress>` element, typed CSS arithmetic, and a one-call `roundRect()` method that simplify UI and canvas work. Enabling the accessibility geometry flag gives assistive tools precise layout data, while the updated Sanitizer API and IndexedDB cursor methods tighten security and data handling. Turn on the `dom_webgl2_enabled` flag to benefit from the new WebGL2 conformance fixes, and consider the MLKEM768-X25519 algorithm for post-quantum cryptography. These concrete additions are ready to use in production builds of Servo today.
